verdict.rationale: RudderStack's docs describe an "open source version" made of a data plane and control plane that depends only on PostgreSQL, so its source can be read. However, community threads describe license churn from SSPL to AGPLv3 and then to the Elastic License, which is source-available rather than OSI-open. That makes the "open license" part of the story uncertain. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the current license and repository location, confirmation that the license is OSI-approved, and coverage of which components (e.g. control plane vs. data plane) are under that license.
